P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No restrictions. The lari is the only legal tender for domestic payments, but foreign exchange may be held as banknotes or on deposit. Proceeds can be converted at market rates and transferred abroad freely.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Foreign exchange may be held on deposit in designated bank accounts, with no restriction on the number of accounts individuals may hold with Georgian banks.

sources.quote: There are no restrictions on the number of bank accounts individuals and enterprises may hold with Georgian banks.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Register as an Individual Entrepreneur (IE) at the Public Service Hall/National Agency of Public Registry. Small Business Status (1% tax) is a separate application through the rs.ge Revenue Service account. Eligibility: sole owner (employees or contractors allowed), turnover under GEL 500,000, and an activity not on the excluded list in Government Ordinance No. 415, which includes consulting, gambling, and medical, architectural and legal professions.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Resident individuals are exempt from tax on income that does not have a Georgian source; the standard PIT is a flat 20%. Individual entrepreneurs with Small Business Status pay 1% of turnover up to GEL 500,000. The rate rises to 3% above that, and the status is cancelled if the cap is exceeded two years running. Micro-business status (turnover under GEL 30,000, no employees) is exempt from tax on business income. Work performed in Georgia for foreign clients is generally Georgian-source, so the foreign-income exemption does not cover it.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Standard VAT is 18%. A person established in Georgia must register as a VAT payer when taxable turnover exceeds GEL 100,000 in any continuous 12-month period. Since April 2021, non-Georgian businesses providing digital services to Georgian consumers must register and charge 18%. Treatment of services exported to foreign business clients was not captured in these sources.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
